project: issue-84 Windows background install for Mohist server and runner
description: Introduce IServiceInstaller abstraction wrapping the existing Linux user-systemd behavior, and add a Windows Scheduled-Task-with-Startup-fallback implementation so the same mo install server|runner / mo server|runner start|stop|restart|status|logs|uninstall surface works on both platforms. Linux behavior must remain byte-identical; --dry-run must preview without writing or executing on either platform.

tasks.title: Promote ServiceInstallOptions and ServiceCommandOptions to top-level internal records
tasks.description: Move the two option records out of SystemdServiceInstaller.cs into their own files (ServiceInstallOptions.cs and ServiceCommandOptions.cs) at the top of the Mohist.Cli namespace. Keep the From(string[]) factory, field order, and parsing behavior identical so existing call sites and tests keep compiling. This unblocks the Windows implementation from sharing the same option types without duplicating the parser.
acceptanceCriteria: packages/cli/Mohist.Cli/ServiceInstallOptions.cs defines an internal sealed record ServiceInstallOptions with the existing field order (DryRun, UnitDir, RepoRoot, ListenUrl, ServerUrl, RunnerRoot) and its From(string[]) factory
packages/cli/Mohist.Cli/ServiceCommandOptions.cs defines an internal sealed record ServiceCommandOptions with the existing field order (DryRun, UnitDir, Lines, Follow) and its From(string[]) factory
SystemdServiceInstaller.cs no longer contains the record declarations; existing call sites and SystemdServiceInstaller internals compile unchanged
The Mohist.Cli assembly builds and the existing InstallSpecs / UpdateSpecs / SystemdInstallDetectorSpecs compile without modification
tasks.output: packages/cli/Mohist.Cli/ServiceInstallOptions.cs and packages/cli/Mohist.Cli/ServiceCommandOptions.cs created; the two records removed from SystemdServiceInstaller.cs
tasks.notes: Design Decision 1: 'ServiceInstallOptions / ServiceCommandOptions are promoted from internal sealed (inside SystemdServiceInstaller.cs) to top-level internal records in their own files'. The From(string[]) factory and --lines/-n / --follow parsing stay unchanged.

Change SystemdServiceInstaller to internal sealed class SystemdServiceInstaller : IServiceInstaller without changing its constructor signature or the public/internal method signatures that command builders and SourceCodeUpdater call. The unit-file render output, systemctl --user argument list, and dry-run output must remain bit-for-bit identical to today.
acceptanceCriteria: packages/cli/Mohist.Cli/IServiceInstaller.cs defines an internal interface with the 14 methods listed in design Decision 1 (InstallServerAsync, InstallRunnerAsync, StartServerAsync, StopServerAsync, RestartServerAsync, StatusServerAsync, LogsServerAsync, UninstallServerAsync, StartRunnerAsync, StopRunnerAsync, RestartRunnerAsync, StatusRunnerAsync, LogsRunnerAsync, UninstallRunnerAsync)

Every method on the interface is implemented by SystemdServiceInstaller

tasks.output: packages/cli/Mohist.Cli/IServiceInstaller.cs created; SystemdServiceInstaller.cs updated to implement it
tasks.notes: Design Decision 7: 'class SystemdServiceInstaller -> class SystemdServiceInstaller : IServiceInstaller. The only change is the class declaration gains the interface. tasks.title: Register IServiceInstaller in DI for both entry points (Linux default)
tasks.description: Update both composition roots (Program.cs and MohistCliCommands.RunAsync in MohistCliCommands.cs) to register IServiceInstaller in the DI container instead of the concrete SystemdServiceInstaller class. On non-Windows runtimes the resolved instance is the existing SystemdServiceInstaller so the Linux path is unchanged. The factory must be a single lambda (services.AddSingleton<IServiceInstaller>(...)) that selects implementation by platform so a later task can flip Windows on by adding a single branch.

MohistCliCommands.RunAsync registers IServiceInstaller via the same factory pattern, using the (output, error, fileSystem, commandExecutor) parameters it already receives

tasks.output: packages/cli/Mohist.Cli/Program.cs and packages/cli/Mohist.Cli/MohistCliCommands.cs updated; IServiceInstaller available from DI on Linux

tasks.title: WindowsScheduledTaskInstaller skeleton and launcher rendering pure helpers
tasks.spec: specs/cli-service-installer/spec.md#Requirement: Windows install writes launcher and registers Scheduled Task; specs/cli-service-installer/spec.md#Requirement: Windows launcher quoting and schtasks argument handling
tasks.description: Create packages/cli/Mohist.Cli/WindowsScheduledTaskInstaller.cs declaring internal sealed class WindowsScheduledTaskInstaller : IServiceInstaller with the same (TextWriter, TextWriter, IFileSystem?, ICommandExecutor?) constructor shape as SystemdServiceInstaller. Implement the rendering pure helpers used by the install flow: RenderServerLauncher(ServerLauncherSpec spec) and RenderRunnerLauncher(RunnerLauncherSpec spec), and the cmd-body quote helper QuoteForCmdBody(string). The server launcher must cd /d to the repo root, set ASPNETCORE_URLS, run dotnet run --project packages\server\src\Mohist.Server\Mohist.Server.csproj, and redirect stdout+stderr to %USERPROFILE%\.mohist\server\out.log. The runner launcher must set SERVER_URL and RUNNER_ROOT, run node packages\runner\dist\cli.js, and redirect to %USERPROFILE%\.mohist\runner\out.log. Paths with spaces (e.g. C:\Users\Mohist User\repos\space repo) must round-trip correctly through QuoteForCmdBody.
acceptanceCriteria: WindowsScheduledTaskInstaller.cs exists with the same constructor signature as SystemdServiceInstaller and implements IServiceInstaller (placeholder bodies are acceptable for the methods implemented in later tasks)

RenderServerLauncher produces content containing 'cd /d <repo-root>', 'set "ASPNETCORE_URLS=<listen-url>"', 'dotnet run --project packages\server\src\Mohist.Server\Mohist.Server.csproj', and '>> "%USERPROFILE%\.mohist\server\out.log" 2>&1'

RenderRunnerLauncher produces content containing 'cd /d <repo-root>', 'set "SERVER_URL=<server-url>"', 'set "RUNNER_ROOT=<runner-root>"', 'node packages\runner\dist\cli.js', and '>> "%USERPROFILE%\.mohist\runner\out.log" 2>&1'

QuoteForCmdBody is a static internal helper that escapes cmd metacharacters (^ caret-escape for & | < > ^ ") and wraps in double quotes when the result contains spaces; a path with spaces round-trips into the launcher without losing characters
tasks.notes: Design Decision 3: 'Launcher rendering and schtasks argument construction are pure functions'. This task implements the .cmd body half. The schtasks /TR half goes in T-007. ServerLauncherSpec and RunnerLauncherSpec records live inside the class.

tasks.title: schtasks argument-array helpers and QuoteForSchtasksTr
tasks.spec: specs/cli-service-installer/spec.md#Requirement: Scheduled Task command generation is testable and argument-safe; specs/cli-service-installer/spec.md#Requirement: Windows launcher quoting and schtasks argument handling
tasks.description: Add the discrete-argument builders to WindowsScheduledTaskInstaller: BuildCreateTaskArgs(TaskCreateSpec spec), BuildRunArgs(string taskName), BuildEndArgs(string taskName), BuildDeleteArgs(string taskName), BuildQueryArgs(string taskName). The /Create args must include /SC ONLOGON, /RL LIMITED, /F, and a /TR that uses QuoteForSchtasksTr (a separate helper from QuoteForCmdBody). The /TR payload must be a single double-quoted string with embedded " escaped as \" per Hermes pattern. Every helper returns string[]; no helper concatenates into a shell string.
acceptanceCriteria: BuildCreateTaskArgs returns an array containing discrete '/Create', '/SC', 'ONLOGON', '/RL', 'LIMITED', '/TN', <task-name>, '/TR', <tr-payload>, '/F' elements in the documented order

BuildRunArgs / BuildEndArgs / BuildDeleteArgs / BuildQueryArgs each return an array with the discrete verb element ('/Run', '/End', '/Delete', '/Query') and a discrete '/TN' element followed by the task name
QuoteForSchtasksTr produces a string different from QuoteForCmdBody for the same input (the spec scenario 'distinct quote helpers' requires the two helpers to produce different outputs)
BuildDeleteArgs includes a discrete '/F' element so the call is non-interactive
No helper returns a string or uses string.Join to assemble the command line; everything is a discrete argument array
tasks.output: Argument-array helpers and QuoteForSchtasksTr added to WindowsScheduledTaskInstaller.cs
tasks.notes: Design Decision 3 second half: 'BuildCreateTaskArgs(TaskCreateSpec spec) -> string[] (the discrete argument list) ... QuoteForCmdBody(string) and QuoteForSchtasksTr(string) -> string (two distinct helpers, per cli-service-installer/spec.md:96-100)'.

tasks.title: Windows install flow: write launcher, register Scheduled Task, fall back to Startup folder
tasks.spec: specs/cli-service-installer/spec.md#Requirement: Windows install writes launcher and registers Scheduled Task; specs/cli-service-installer/spec.md#Requirement: Windows falls back to Startup-folder launcher when Scheduled Task is blocked; specs/cli-service-installer/spec.md#Requirement: Windows install honors --repo-root, --listen-url, --server-url, and --runner-root
tasks.description: Implement InstallServerAsync and InstallRunnerAsync on WindowsScheduledTaskInstaller. The flow is: resolve launcher spec (repo root from --repo-root or default Mohist.sln walk, listen/server URLs, log path); render and write ~/.mohist/service/mohist-<kind>.cmd using the helper from T-006; build schtasks /Create args with the helper from T-007 and call them via ICommandExecutor.ExecuteAsync('schtasks', args). When /Create exits non-zero, fall back to writing a Startup-folder .cmd shortcut at %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\Mohist_<Server|Runner>.cmd whose body is a single 'call "<launcher>"' line and record 'startup-fallback' in the installer metadata file (~/.mohist/service/mohist-<kind>.install.json). --dry-run must preview launcher path, launcher summary, the schtasks argument list, and 'would use Startup-fallback if Scheduled Task creation is blocked' without writing files or running commands.
acceptanceCriteria: InstallServerAsync writes ~/.mohist/service/mohist-server.cmd with the rendered server launcher (using the helper from T-006) and then attempts schtasks /Create /SC ONLOGON /RL LIMITED /TN Mohist_Server /TR <launcher> /F
InstallRunnerAsync writes ~/.mohist/service/mohist-runner.cmd and attempts schtasks /Create /SC ONLOGON /RL LIMITED /TN Mohist_Runner /TR <launcher> /F

When schtasks /Create exits non-zero, the installer writes the Startup-folder .cmd shortcut whose body invokes the generated launcher (no inline server/runner command) and writes the installer metadata recording startup-fallback
The default --repo-root discovery walks up from AppContext.BaseDirectory looking for Mohist.sln (matches Linux behavior); --listen-url, --server-url, --runner-root override the launcher env values

With --dry-run: no file is written, no process is spawned (FakeCommandExecutor.ExecutedCommands is empty), and the output preview contains the install path, a launcher summary line, the schtasks argument list, and a fallback line
tasks.output: InstallServerAsync and InstallRunnerAsync fully implemented on WindowsScheduledTaskInstaller
tasks.notes: Design Decision 4: 'Install flow: write launcher first, then attempt Scheduled Task, then fall back'. The installer metadata file at ~/.mohist/service/mohist-<kind>.install.json records which backend was used so uninstall and lifecycle know what to do.

tasks.title: Windows lifecycle ops: start, stop, restart, status, logs, uninstall for server and runner
tasks.spec: specs/cli-service-installer/spec.md#Requirement: Windows start, stop, and restart use the right backend; specs/cli-service-installer/spec.md#Requirement: Windows status reports install state and live runtime state; specs/cli-service-installer/spec.md#Requirement: Windows logs read generated log files; specs/cli-service-installer/spec.md#Requirement: Windows uninstall cleans up install artifacts but preserves user data; specs/cli-service-installer/spec.md#Requirement: --dry-run previews without writing or executing
tasks.description: Implement the remaining 12 IServiceInstaller methods on WindowsScheduledTaskInstaller. A shared DetectBackend helper (private, tested through behavior) consults installer metadata and the Startup-folder file to pick scheduled-task / startup-fallback / launcher-only. start with scheduled-task calls schtasks /Run; with fallback/launcher-only starts the generated launcher as a detached process (UseShellExecute=true, CreateNoWindow=true). stop calls schtasks /End when a task is present and ends matching PIDs (taskkill /F) when fallback/launcher-only is in use; never deletes the task on stop. restart = stop + start. status reports install registration (task / fallback / launcher file presence) plus live runtime state. logs reads %USERPROFILE%\.mohist\<server|runner>\out.log with bounded tail -n and FileSystemWatcher-based --follow. uninstall deletes the scheduled task (if present), the Startup-folder shortcut, the generated .cmd, and the installer metadata — never the database, config, worktrees, or log files. --dry-run for each prints the actions and argument lists without writing or executing.
acceptanceCriteria: StartServerAsync / StartRunnerAsync: when installer metadata says scheduled-task, the fake executor records a schtasks /Run call with /TN Mohist_Server or Mohist_Runner; when metadata says startup-fallback, a Process.Start is recorded against the generated launcher path

StopServerAsync / StopRunnerAsync: when scheduled-task is present, the fake executor records schtasks /End; matching PIDs are taskkill'd when fallback/launcher-only is in use; the task is never deleted on stop
RestartServerAsync / RestartRunnerAsync call Stop then Start with the same backend selection

StatusServerAsync / StatusRunnerAsync output includes install registration lines (scheduled-task: yes/no, startup-fallback: yes/no, launcher file: present/missing) and live runtime state; server status additionally reports the http://localhost:3456/api/health reachability

LogsServerAsync reads %USERPROFILE%\.mohist\server\out.log and prints the trailing options.Lines lines; LogsRunnerAsync reads %USERPROFILE%\.mohist\runner\out.log; -n 200 bounds the output to at most 200 lines; --follow uses FileSystemWatcher + CancellationToken and stops on Ctrl+C (CancellationToken registration asserted via a 200ms timeout in tests)

UninstallServerAsync / UninstallRunnerAsync remove the scheduled task, the Startup-folder shortcut, the generated .cmd, and the installer metadata; a separately-added mohist.db and out.log remain in the fake filesystem after uninstall
Every lifecycle method honors --dry-run: no fake command executions, no file writes, and a preview line that names the backend and the action
tasks.output: All 12 remaining IServiceInstaller methods implemented on WindowsScheduledTaskInstaller
tasks.notes: Design Decision 5: 'Lifecycle actions are backend-aware ... DetectBackend consults schtasks /Query + Startup-folder file presence'. Design Decision 6: 'Uninstall ... never touches user data'. The --follow FileSystemWatcher design uses a CancellationToken registered on Console.CancelKeyPress; tests inject a fake watcher / token source.
